statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON (green). Tail 12% (low), Stress 37% (moderate), Confidence 86% (high). Shared assessment for NQ futures and NAS100 CFD.
recommendation: Tail remains well below the block threshold, so the mapped state is EA_ON. Conditional risk is concentrated in a narrow 13:30-15:00 UTC band spanning the U.S. cash open, the Richmond Fed survey and the Williams and Jefferson remarks; that band is published as the danger window rather than the whole session. A second, lighter checkpoint sits at the 17:00 UTC 2-year auction and Barkin remarks. Existing-position management and emergency protection logic are unaffected by this mapping. This is a descriptive market-regime assessment, not personal financial advice.
headline: Nasdaq-100 futures hold a mid-range recovery after the overnight dip was bought back; low volatility and functioning retracement keep tail risk low into the U.S. open and the Fed-speaker block
body: Monday closed with the Nasdaq-100 cash index at a record 30,482.35, up 2.83%, inside a 29,933.22-30,557.33 day range, as an AI and semiconductor rally lifted the Nasdaq Composite about 2.3% to a record and the S&P 500 about 1.5%. Leadership was concentrated: AMD reached an all-time high above $610 and a $1 trillion market value, Intel gained about 12%, Arm about 10%, Meta about 11% on the reception of its Muse app, and the PHLX semiconductor index rose more than 3%. Overnight, NQ Dec-26 futures fell to 30,670.00, recovered the entire give-back and now trade near 30,820.75, up 0.12% against a 30,784.75 prior settlement, inside a 30,670.00-30,916.50 range. A dip that is bought back in full and then holds mid-to-upper range is direct evidence that retracement is functioning, which is the main reason Tail stays at 12 rather than rising with the index into record territory. VIX at 14.80, down 0.47% in a 14.64-14.95 range, confirms the absence of a volatility bid. Crude has fallen for a fifth consecutive session to a two-week low, with WTI near 89.85, down 2.56%, on reporting that Iran could reopen the Strait of Hormuz if the U.S. lifted its blockade of Iranian ports and that Trump is open to meeting Iran's president at the UN General Assembly; U.S. Central Command has described Hormuz flows at a six-month high with transit lanes clear. That diplomacy is unresolved and two-sided, so it is scored as a Stress and headline channel rather than as directional evidence. The unresolved macro tension remains rates: the 10-year yield sits near 4.96% after easing below 5% on Monday, the 2-year is 4.76% against an effective funds rate of 3.88%, and the debate about whether further tightening is needed is live, which is why Stress holds in the moderate band at 37 while equities print records. Shared delayed cross-asset context shows megacaps modestly higher on the latest session, 6 of 8 positive with a mean of about +0.30%, against semiconductors 5 of 7 lower with a mean of about -0.19%; that mild rotation away from Monday's chip leadership is a consolidation signal and specifically not the aligned one-way confirmation that would justify a higher Tail. The Finviz futures and calendar sections were unavailable in the latest collection, so cross-asset futures alignment could not be checked from that feed and Confidence is set at 86 rather than higher. Today's scheduled catalysts are the 13:30 UTC cash open, the Richmond Fed manufacturing survey at 14:00 UTC, Williams at 14:05 UTC and Vice Chair Jefferson at 14:20 UTC, then the 2-year note auction and Barkin at 17:00 UTC; Wednesday brings the high-impact S&P Global flash PMIs at 13:45 UTC. None of those has printed, so their importance is carried as conditional Stress rather than as observed structure. Mapped policy state: EA_ON, with the narrow 13:30-15:00 UTC danger window published as the concentrated conditional band.

lookbackSummary: The past 24 hours contain a complete set of 24 published hourly assessments. Tail built steadily through Monday's U.S. session as the index trended to a record close, peaking at 33 with Stress at 57 during the 19:00 UTC hour, which mapped to BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES from 14:00 through 19:00 UTC. After the cash close the trend-up characterisation gave way to a normal, two-way regime: Tail dropped to 23 at 20:00 UTC, to 14 at 21:00 UTC and into a 11-13 band for every overnight hour since, with Stress easing from the mid-50s to the low-to-mid 30s. The overnight dip to 30,670.00 and its full recovery is the clearest single piece of evidence in the window that mean reversion is currently working.
outlookSummary: The 24-hour outlook keeps Tail inside an 10-18 band, so every forecast hour maps to EA_ON. Conditional risk is front-loaded into the 13:30-15:00 UTC band covering the cash open, the Richmond Fed survey and the Williams and Jefferson remarks, where Tail peaks at 18 and Stress at 48, with a lighter secondary checkpoint at the 17:00 UTC 2-year auction and Barkin remarks and again in the power hour into the 20:00 UTC close. Overnight the profile decays to a session low of 10 through the Asian hours before rebuilding modestly into Wednesday's European session ahead of the high-impact flash PMIs at 13:45 UTC. Confidence falls from 86 to 60 across the horizon because no current evidence constrains a path a full day ahead. Every post-current-hour figure is conditional risk; no future price structure has been observed.
